conviction_note: The FY27 guide is the first formal one since the October 2025 guide reset (-54%). The evidence pulls both ways. On the negative side: a count-date enrollment headwind (Q4 exit of 234.2K, a ~12K-student Texas school lost, applications behind) and a new CEO's first guide. On the positive side: a low Q1 bar, conversion and re-registration running ahead, an activist-driven capital allocation review, the CEO's stated buyback intent when the window opens in late October, and 19% of shares short at 10.5 days to cover. So p_up sits at 52, against a large abs_move of 15 anchored on the 15.8% option-implied move. The findings sum to +1.5 and the scaled number is +0.6. The gap is because the scaled number carries all the sign uncertainty.
bar: Q1 FY27 (Sep quarter) consensus is EPS $1.07 on revenue $612.25M, against $1.52 / $620.88M a year ago, per MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-20-stride-inc-stock/ and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-stride-lrn-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/). That bar is DISPUTED: a single-analyst aggregator figure is EPS $1.32 on revenue $647M (https://www.tickflow.io/stock/LRN/forecast). The FY27 bar is also unresolved: MarketBeat has FY EPS at $8.62, a German aggregator has FY27 revenue at ~$2.7B (https://aktien.guide/kursziel/Stride-Inc-US86333M1080), and there is no enrollment consensus. The company gave no FY27 guide in August, only revenue per enrollment 'relatively flat to up slightly' and gross margin, capex and SG&A % 'flattish' (https://s26.q4cdn.com/126400783/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Stride_4Q26_Transcript.pdf). Because both bars are disputed, every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is crowded. FINRA via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/lrn/shortinterest) shows 7,968,668 shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~19.2% of 41.56M shares outstanding, with 10.45 days to cover. That is up from 6.64M at 07-31 and 8.02M at 09-15 (11.68 days to cover). The baseline 25-delta skew is +1.87 vol points (mild put bid), and priced_direction_lean reads 'balanced'. Put/call open interest is 0.63, ATM IV 73.5%, and the event-implied move 15.77%. Spot is 80.78, -47% from the 52-week high, +2.65% over 20 days and -2.68% over 5 days. Sell-side: 2 Buy / 5 Hold, consensus target $108.75. BMO cut its target from $93 to $90 on Oct 5, and William Blair downgraded on 2026-07-30. No open-market insider buying since July (Form 4s are grants and withholding only, https://www.quantisnow.com/insiders/LRN).

findings.finding: The count-date enrollment comparison is structurally hard. Q4 FY26 average enrollment exited at 234.2K (-0.5% y/y), and the CFO said Q1 count-date growth 'will face a more difficult comparison' because there is no carryover from FY26 in-year growth. Barrington's on-call arithmetic: the same +12.4K Q4-to-Q1 add as last year leaves Q1 at -0.4% y/y. That arithmetic starts from a base that still includes Lone Star Online Academy (~12,000 students, about 5% of enrollment), which Roscoe ISD did not renew for 2026-27. Some of those families are being moved to Texas Virtual Academy, and K-2 families to a tuition-free (zero-revenue) private online school. Applications are 'slightly behind last year'. Consensus Q1 revenue of $612.25M (-1.4%) implies enrollment roughly -2% at flat revenue per enrollment. A full LSOA loss net of re-placement points to -3% to -5%, so the risk to the count and to the FY27 enrollment guide is to the downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The enrollment/guide line has produced this name's largest moves. 2025-10-28 was -54.4%, when Q1 count enrollment came in below plan on platform problems and the FY guide was cut. 2026-01-27 was +14.3%, and 2025-08-05 was +15.7%, on the guides of those quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: The LSOA headcount (~12K) comes from a Houston Chronicle story that sell-side previews do not cite. If the market fully priced a 3-5% enrollment decline, consensus revenue would sit near $600M rather than $612M, and FY27 EPS consensus would not be $8.62 (above FY26's $8.33). Partly priced: the stock is -47% from its high and the skew is mildly put-bid.
findings.independence: LSOA size and placement terms: Houston Chronicle via GovTech, 2026-06-26 (https://www.govtech.com/education/k-12/sudden-closure-of-texas-online-school-surprises-12k-students), a different source from the transcript. Q4 enrollment: company release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm). The 19% short interest and 10.5 days to cover shrink this negative.

findings.finding: Management's own leading indicators were positive on 2026-08-04. Conversion metrics are improved, and re-registration is 'tracking slightly ahead of last year'. The CFO said 'we're not going to have all the windows closed to the same extent' as FY26, so in-year enrollment growth should return. Partner-state budgets are finalised and 'the overall funding environment remains supportive'. Revenue per enrollment is guided 'relatively flat to up slightly'. Asked whether fall expectations differ from the Q2/Q3 calls, the CFO answered 'I think it's fair'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-04 print with this commentary moved +2.65%. That came after a -15% move on 07-30 on the CEO change and preliminary data.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is public and inside what the company already said. What is not priced is whether August and September ('our busiest months') converted. If the market believed in-year growth resumes, the stock would not sit at ~11x P/E, near its 50-day average of $81.98.
findings.independence: Same document as the count-date finding, but a different statement (leading indicators versus the starting base). Peer demand for virtual school is strong in Pearson's H1 (separate finding).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 Stride signed a cooperation agreement with activist Fivespan Partners (founder Dylan Haggart, ex-ValueAct partner) and formed a Capital Allocation Committee co-chaired by Haggart. The committee will 'review the company's capital structure' and publish a target capital structure and cash-flow allocation framework within ~3 months. Stride holds $1,034M of cash and securities (~30% of its ~$3.4B market cap) and $311M of remaining buyback authorization. In August the CEO said: 'Once our trading window opens at the end of October, I intend to actively consider opportunistic stock repurchases.' The window opens right after this print, so buyback or recapitalisation language on the call is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has turned on capital return. FY26 Q4 buybacks of ~$100M accompanied a +2.65% reaction. The stock did not visibly rally on the 10-09 announcement: it opened at $84.32 on 10-13 and is at $80.78 now.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is lower since the 10-09 release (5-day run-up -2.68%), so the market has not paid for a recap or accelerated buyback. A priced recap would show as a post-announcement rally and a call-skewed surface. The skew is instead mildly put-bid.
findings.independence: The CEO's buyback-window statement is in a separate document, the Aug 4 transcript (https://s26.q4cdn.com/126400783/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Stride_4Q26_Transcript.pdf). Cooperation-agreement terms (Haggart joins the board Oct 30; nominations withdrawn) per https://finviz.com/news/400803/stride-to-appoint-steven-guttentag-and-dylan-haggart-to-board-of-directors-and-form-capital-allocation-committee.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 6.64M shares (07-31) to 7.97M (09-30), ~19% of shares outstanding at 10.45 days to cover. That is a crowded short into a guide print where the Q1 bar is low (EPS consensus -30% y/y). Any guide that is not a reset forces covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the -54% October 2025 reset, the next three guide-bearing prints moved +14.3%, +2.8% and +2.7%, and none was down. No measured squeeze history for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The squeeze is conditional on the guide, so it is not in spot. Short interest is still building, not covering (8.02M at 09-15, 7.97M at 09-30), which means the shorts expect a weak guide. If shorts were being covered ahead of the print, short interest would be falling.
findings.independence: Mildly put-bid skew (+1.87) from the baseline. Earlier figure from the same provider: 6.6M shares, 16% of float, on 2026-08-19.

findings.finding: The largest direct competitor, Pearson's Connections Academy (Virtual Learning), reported in H1 2026 (2026-07-31) that spring-semester 2025/26 enrolment growth accelerated to 15%. Sales were +19% underlying, all 10 long-term contract renewals succeeded, and 5 new schools open for 2026/27 (46 schools, 32 states), citing 'strong demand for virtual schooling'. That points to healthy category demand going into fall 2026, though it may also be share taken from Stride (Stride Q4 enrollment -0.5%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction of LRN to Pearson prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy that reported before Stride's August call, so it is largely priced. It is included because it is the only independent demand series for fall 2026 found. The sign is ambiguous (category demand up versus a share shift).
findings.independence: Proxy only; it does not confirm Stride's own count. Pearson's 2025 full-year results said 'preliminary market share data indicates that we are gaining share', which cuts against Stride.

findings.finding: The Q1 reported-quarter bar is low. Consensus EPS of $1.07 is down 30% from $1.52 a year ago, on revenue of $612.25M (-1.4%). Stride beat EPS consensus in 7 of its last 8 quarters, including a $2.12 versus $1.64 beat in Q4 FY26 on revenue of $636.1M versus ~$626.5M. The CFO guided gross margin, SG&A % and capex flattish, with no large known one-off cost in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have not been rewarded on their own. The Q4 FY26 EPS beat of $0.48 got +2.65%, and the Q1 FY26 beat ($1.52 vs $1.23) came with a -54% move on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a habit of beating. Capped small because the bar is disputed (a tickflow single-analyst figure of $1.32 / $647M) and the stock trades on the guide, not the quarter.
findings.independence: Q4 actuals are in the company's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm).

findings.finding: This is the new CEO's first guide. Bob Knowling was installed immediately on 2026-07-29 after a 'board-led' change: the stock fell ~15% that day and William Blair downgraded to market perform. BMO trimmed its target to $90 (from $93) on 2026-10-05, just ahead of the print. There is a 'reset the base' risk for FY27, given the August claim of being 'on track to achieve our FY 2028 financial targets', which were set in 2023 at $2.7-3.3B revenue against $2.52B in FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-10-28 guide reset moved -54.4%. The 2026-07-30 CEO change moved -15.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced in the -15% CEO-change drop and the -47% from the high. What is not priced is whether the new CEO uses the first guide to lower the FY28 targets. If that were priced, the FY27 EPS consensus would be below FY26 rather than $8.62.
findings.independence: BMO target cut per https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-stride-lrn-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/. The CEO said the change had 'no consideration about ... forward-looking performance' (Aug 4 transcript), which cuts against this finding and is why it is sized small. The crowded short also shrinks it.

outside_window.finding: The Capital Allocation Committee's target capital structure and cash-flow framework is promised 'within approximately three months' of 2026-10-09, i.e. around January 2027. A leveraged buyback or special return would land then unless pre-announced on the call.
Pearson's 2026 nine-month trading update, the first read of Connections Academy's fall 2026/27 enrolments, is due 2026-10-22, after the exit window.
Dylan Haggart (Fivespan) joins the board on 2026-10-30; the annual meeting is on 2026-12-10.

baseline_tension: Neither side clearly wins. The mildly put-bid skew (+1.87) and building short interest agree with the enrollment-headwind negative. The crowded short (19%, 10.5 days to cover), the low bar, the activist capital review and the -47% drawdown argue the downside is well owned. So p_up is held near 50 and the large implied move is kept as the scale.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: MarketBeat $1.07/$612M vs tickflow $1.32/$647M, and FY27 bar unsourced): enrollment-guide finding capped from -2.0 to -1.5, and reported-quarter beat finding from +0.8 to +0.5
Rule 6 (inside what the company already guided): the conversion/re-registration finding moved toward 0, from +1.0 to +0.5
Rule 7 (crowded short, 19% at 10.5 days to cover): new-CEO reset negative shrunk from -1.0 to -0.7
Rule 5 (proxy): Pearson peer finding shrunk from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 6 (exit window): capital-allocation framework kept out of findings in outside_window; the capital-return finding trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2 so it counts only call commentary inside the window
Positioning finding trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2: the squeeze depends on the same guide the negatives rest on, so p_up moved from 53 to 52
